textbookText: 2. Oviducts: These are paired, white, long, much convoluted and internally glandular and ciliated tubes lying one on either side of the body cavity. Each oviduct consists of oviducal funnel, tubular part and ovisac (uterus). By the rupture of ovarian follicles, the ova are released into body cavity which is called ovulation and ova reach the oviducal funnels through ostia (mouth of funnel). Then, they move through tubules and stored in the ovisac. Beating of cilia on the inner wall of oviduct facilitates the movement of ova. Ova are coated externally by the albuminous secretion while passing via oviduct. Ova are released at the time of amplexus. A mature female frog can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilization is external. Development is indirect involving a larval stage called tadpole. 3. Cloacal chamber and cloaca: Cloacal chamber is the median sac between hind limbs that opens outside by cloacal opening. Ova are discharged to water through cloaca during or after amplex or amplexus.

Figure 8.4.36 Unfertilized egg of frog Amplexus: Under the influence of testosterone hormone, development of copulatory or nuptial pads, vocal sacs and formation of sperms takes place in the male frog during breeding season. Basal part of first finger or index finger of male is enlarged or swollen to form copulatory pad. With the help of vocal sac, male frog is capable of producing croaking sound which attracts the nearby female frog. Then male frog mount on the back of female and grasp female’s abdomen firmly which is called sexual embrace. Then, female frog is stimulated and lays eggs in water in the form of spawn and milt is discharged over it by male. Fertilization occurs which is followed by embryonic development.
